summary: Louisiana has no law that expressly prohibits keeping a captive-bred roof rat. The 'potentially dangerous wild quadruped' ban (LAC 76:V-115) covers only big cats, bears, wolves, and primates; the 'outlaw quadruped' list is feral hogs, coyotes, and armadillos — no rodents. Both state and local definitions of 'wild or exotic animal' carve out 'laboratory rats... bred and raised in captivity which have never known the wild' and common 'pocket pets,' which a multi-generation captive-bred roof rat fits. So keeping, breeding, and giving are effectively legal, though R. rattus isn't named by species. The live edge is commercial sale: whether LDWF treats it as a 'nongame quadruped' needing a breeder license (29... §56:262) is unsettled — confirm before selling. Parish ordinances vary; never release one.

keep.why: R. rattus is on no Louisiana prohibited/dangerous list: the 'potentially dangerous wild quadruped' rule (LAC 76:V-115) lists only big cats/bears/wolves/primates, and 'outlaw quadrupeds' (RS 56:116.2) are feral hogs/coyotes/armadillos. Both state and local 'wild or exotic animal' definitions carve out 'laboratory rats bred and raised in captivity which have never known the wild' and 'pocket pets,' which a captive-bred roof rat fits. Effectively legal, but R. rattus isn't named by species and no LDWF guidance confirms the carve-out reaches it — hence unclear.
keep.governing_law: LAC 76:V-115 (dangerous quadrupeds — no rodents); RS 56:116.2 (outlaw quadrupeds); RS 56:8 / local 'wild or exotic animal' definitions (laboratory-rat carve-out).

breed.why: Because keeping is unregulated/unclear, private hobby breeding of captive-born stock falls outside any explicit prohibition. The nongame-quadruped breeder license (RS 56:262) targets wild/fur-associated quadrupeds; a captive-bred non-native commensal rodent not taken from the wild sits in a definitional gap. No-release obligation applies (RS 56:20).

sell_give.why: Non-commercial giving/rehoming appears to need no permit. Commercial SALE may require a Nongame Quadruped Breeder License (RS 56:262, ~$25/yr) IF LDWF classifies R. rattus as a 'nongame quadruped' — an unresolved question. A commercially-minded seller should get a written LDWF determination first; free vetted adoption avoids the issue.
sell_give.governing_law: RS 56:262; RS 56:32 (penalties for unlicensed wildlife commerce).

transport.why: No rule specifically restricts intrastate transport of captive-bred R. rattus. Louisiana's animal-health import rules (LAC 7:XXI) cover dogs/cats (CVI + rabies) and livestock/poultry, not pet rodents; the 'wild or semi-wild animal' import-report rule likely doesn't apply because captive-bred lab-type rats are excluded from 'wild or exotic animal.' So no CVI appears required — confirm with the State Vet. Never release (RS 56:20).
transport.governing_law: LAC 7:XXI-571 (dogs/cats CVI — N/A to rodents); RS 56:20 (no-release).

restrictions.summary: Commercial sale MAY require a Louisiana Nongame Quadruped Breeder License (RS 56:262) if LDWF classifies R. rattus as a 'nongame quadruped' — unsettled, so get a written determination before advertising for sale. Free/private rehoming needs no permit. Parish ordinances may add limits.
steps: Ask LDWF whether captive-bred R. rattus is a 'nongame quadruped' needing a §56:262 license
restrictions.where_to_file: Louisiana Dept of Wildlife & Fisheries (Wildlife Permits)

restrictions.summary: Never release a roof rat (RS 56:20). Parish/municipal ordinances (e.g., Orleans Parish §6-100) define 'wild or exotic animal' and may add local rules — check your parish.

inquiry_focus: Does LDWF classify captive-bred Rattus rattus as a 'nongame quadruped' subject to the RS 56:262 breeder/exhibitor license — i.e., does the definition reach a non-native commensal rodent kept purely as a pet, or does the 'laboratory rats... bred and raised in captivity which have never known the wild' carve-out (in state and local 'wild or exotic animal' definitions) exclude it? If a license is needed for commercial sale, what are the terms? Separately, does the Dept of Agriculture & Forestry require a CVI or 10-day import report to bring a captive-bred pet rat into Louisiana?
